newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims unchanged in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims unchanged in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans filing for first-time jobless benefits held steady last week, the government reported Thursday, but the level of claims remained in a range that analysts say reflects a strong economy.
The Labour Department said weekly jobless claims were unchanged at 322,000 in the week ended May 24. Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 321,000 for the latest week.
Economists typically view claims at the low end of the 300,000 range as suggestive of a firm labour market.
Claims have been on a downswing in recent weeks after spiking upward earlier this spring because of special factors such as Midwestern flooding and auto industry strikes.
The four-week moving average of claims, which smoothes out fluctuations in the weekly data, fell to 327,500 from 333,500.
The total number of Americans continuing to claim unemployment benefits rose by 15,000 to 2,288,000 in the week ended May 17, the latest week for which those data were available.
The department said five states reported decreases exceeding 1,000 claims on an unadjusted basis in the week ended May 17, the latest period for which data were available.
They were California, with 3,327 fewer claims; North Carolina, down 2,768; New York, off 1,898; Pennsylvania, down 1,866; and Michigan, off 1,521.
California reported fewer layoffs in the service industry and in agriculture while North Carolina reported fewer layoffs in the construction and textile industries.

Pennsylvania said it had fewer layoffs in the trade, chemical and fabricated metals industries while Michigan said it had fewer layoffs in various industries throughout the state. New York had no comment.
There were four states reporting increases exceeding 1,000 claims on an unadjusted basis, in the May 17 week.
They were Louisiana, with 1,857 additional claims; Kentucky, with 1,612; Missouri, with 1,440; and Mississippi, with 1,237.
Louisiana reported layoffs in the transportation equipment industry while Kentucky said it had layoffs in the service and electrical equipment industries.
Missouri reported layoffs in the trade, service and transportation industries. Mississippi had layoffs in the service industry.
